memory_raw.text: Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.
Nessa draws Roan aside to talk.
Nessa: have a child with me — I'll put in 1 of 3 food.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

The pile's gone and I got nothing — I was too slow and now I'm sitting at zero food with a year to survive on it. Tell me you got something before the quick hands cleared it, and tell me you're not planning to carry me the whole year because I won't have that.

Father, I got nothing from the pile either — we're both at zero from there, but I came into the year with four held over, so I'm at four total. Take one from me right now; you need to eat before anything else, and one food isn't the difference between my safety and yours.

I'll take it, and I won't pretend I don't need it — but that's the last I take from you this year unless the ground falls out from under both of us. Four is thin enough as it is; you hold the rest and you watch who's sitting heavy, because Kael pulled three from the pile and Zinn took three more, and one of those two is going to draw eyes before the year is out.

Kael I can read — he's old and careful and three from the pile is a man making sure he eats, not a man building something. Zinn is the one that sits wrong with me; she's Mako's blood, she's got his strength, and if those two are moving together they're the most dangerous pair in this village right now. I'm going to find Nessa before nightfall and ask her what she's seen of Zinn's loyalties, because we need to know whether she's ours or his before we find out the hard way.

Nessa's the right door — she's fed you four times and she gave to Zinn directly, so she's got a read on that girl that we don't. But go careful with how you ask it; Nessa's Bram's blood too, and a question about Zinn's loyalties can double as a question about her own. Come back to me before you do anything with what she tells you.

I'll come back to you before I move — that's a promise. But father, you're at one food now and the year is long; if Nessa can't tell me what I need to know about Zinn, my next step is asking Sela directly, because she carried that girl and she watches everything. Don't let your count drop below one before I'm back.

Sela's the right second door and I trust her read — but I want to name something before you go: Dell's sitting on eight food and she's had nothing from Bram's circle in two years, which means she's either very clean or very careful, and either way she's worth a word. Don't let Zinn be the only name we're chasing while something quieter builds at Dell's end.

Dell's eight is a number I can't explain and that bothers me more than Zinn's three — a woman that well-fed with no obvious source is either very good at hiding it or very good at building something we haven't seen yet. I'll put that name in my mouth when I talk to Nessa, see if she's heard anything from Bram's side about Dell's dealings. You stay above one and I'll be back before the light changes.
Go, then — and tell nobody where you're headed or what you're asking, not even Kael. If someone asks why you're moving, you're checking on Sela. That's all.

Roan, you've got nothing in your hands and I've got six, and I'm not here to hold that over you — I'm here because Dell and I trust you more than we trust the direction Mako's circle is pulling, and I want to know whether that trust runs both ways before this year gets loud.

Ryn, I'm listening and I won't pretend the timing doesn't help — but before I say whether the trust runs both ways, I want to know what changed, because last year I watched you stand with Dell and Dav when they stripped Esa's food, and that's not a small thing to step past. Tell me what you're offering and what you want back, and I'll tell you where I stand.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Ryn just handed Dell two food without blinking, which means that cluster is feeding itself now and not looking our way — so I want to know, before the day gets older, whether the three of you are still standing where you were, because I've got five food and I'm not spending any of it until I know who's next to me when Mako decides quiet is over.

Kael, I'm standing where I always was — and yes, Ryn feeding Dell while Bram's already been talking to Mako this morning is the thing I'd have led with if you hadn't. We've got a decision to make before those two circles find each other: do we move first, or do we wait and count who shows up?

Taric's right that we don't want Bram and Mako finding each other before we've named what we're doing — but I'll say what I said to Bram this morning: Dell holds eight food and eighty-five strength, and moving on her without Mako in our count is a fight I don't survive even if we win. Kael, you've got five food and you're the strongest man I'd trust — what do you need from us to make this worth your step forward?

Esa, I'm not moving on Dell — not this year, not with Mako's strength unaccounted for and Zinn already eating out of his hand. What I need from the three of you is simpler: Roan, you've got a son with Sela, which means you've got a door into Mako's world that none of us have — go find out whether he sees us as neighbors or prey, because everything else we decide today hangs on that answer.

Roan, Kael's right — your blood through Eron is the only thread into that household that doesn't look like calculation, and we need that thread pulled today, not tomorrow. While you go, I want Kael and Esa to tell me plainly: if Roan comes back with word that Mako's already decided we're prey, what are we actually willing to do about it, because I'm fifty-one with thirty-eight strength and I need to know I'm standing next to people who've made that decision before the moment arrives.

Taric, I'll say it plain: if Mako's already counted us as prey, we don't fight him with four bodies and a hundred and sixty-five strength against his eighty-three — we bring in Bram's fifty-eight first, even if it costs us, because the alternative is losing before we start. The price of Bram's help is the thing I've been turning over, and I don't love it, but I love starving less.

Kael's right about Bram being the price — but I want to know what price before we pay it, because a man who tried to raid this village once and walked away empty doesn't come cheap when he thinks he's needed. Roan, go to Eron first, not Sela, not Mako — your son will tell you true before he thinks to protect anyone else. Come back fast.

Taric named the price question right, and I'll add the shape of it: Bram will want to know he's first among equals when this settles, and if we let him believe that without ever saying it aloud, we buy the alliance without signing the contract. Roan, go to Eron now — every minute we spend talking is a minute Bram's already in Mako's ear.

Roan, move — and when you find Eron, ask him where Mako was standing when Zinn took three from the pile this morning, because a man who lets his newborn daughter hoard while the rest of us scramble isn't thinking like a neighbor. Esa, Taric — while he goes, I want us to sit with one question: if Bram's already in Mako's ear, what does he want to hear, and can we make sure he hears something different from us first.
Dell gathers Roan, Ryn to talk.

Roan, you've got nothing in your hands and a son who needs to eat, and Ryn and I are standing here with food and the same answer we had when Bram came for you the first time — so I want to say plain what we're building before Mako gets here with a prettier version of the same offer.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Dav is dead and his household is loose — Ryn and Dell are still moving together, but they've got no man behind them now and Mako's been feeding Zinn quietly for months, which means he's already thinking about what comes next. I want to know who in this room saw that raid on Esa coming, and whether any of you are willing to say plainly that we don't let the next one go unanswered.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

I saw it coming the moment Dav started moving food toward Ryn instead of spreading it — a man consolidating his household is a man building something, and Esa was the nearest soft target. What I want to know is whether we're naming Mako the next problem or whether we're still pretending that a man who just fathered two children in this village by two different women is just being quiet.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Esa, Bram wants to hear that Mako's circling him too — that's the only thing that moves a man like that faster than greed, and it has the advantage of being mostly true. So before Roan's back, I want one of us to find Bram and plant that seed plainly: not a threat, not a deal, just a word in passing that Mako's been quiet in a way that should make everyone nervous.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Mako's not being quiet — he's been counting, and two children by two women means two households that answer to him whether they know it yet or not. If we're going to name him the problem, I want to hear it from each of you plainly, because when the moment comes I'm not going to be the only one who said it first.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Bram, I've fed you three times over the years and I've never asked for more than the door staying open — I'm asking now: if Mako moves on anyone in this room, will you stand with us, and I want your answer before the others give theirs, because yours is the one that decides the weight of the rest.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Bram, the room's still waiting and I'm not going to let it fill with my own voice again — you've heard what I'm asking, you know what I've given, and a man who doesn't answer when the question's this plain has already answered.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Zinn, Roan, Vela, Ryn, Mako, Nessa, Sela, Esa, Eron, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 705).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Vela gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Bram just tried to take from me and the whole village shut him down — every last one of them, even Mako — and I want us to sit with what that means before we decide it's over. A man who swings and misses that badly either goes quiet for good or finds a smarter way the next time, and I'd rather we name which one Bram is before he's had time to decide himself.
Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone again and Mako walked off with five — I counted — which means he's feeding Zinn and Sela and still sitting pretty while the rest of us scrape. Taric, Roan, you're both at zero food right now, and I've got four, so I'm not going to watch you starve when I can prevent it — but I need to know first whether either of you has heard anything from Bram since he pulled back last year, because a man who tests the water once tests it again.

Bram's been quiet since the village turned on him, and quiet like that usually means a man's either broken or calculating — I haven't spoken to him directly, but I've watched him feed Nessa three times yesterday which tells me he's still thinking about what comes after him, not just himself. Kael, I'll take whatever you can spare, and I'll owe it when it matters — but the thing that worries me more than Bram right now is Mako walking away with five while Roan and I stand here with nothing, because a man that well-fed in a village this size isn't planning to stay comfortable, he's planning to stay in front.

Kael, give me one food and I'll hold the rest of the conversation until I'm sure I'm alive to finish it — then we talk about Mako, because Taric's right that five from the pile isn't eating, it's positioning, and a man positioning that hard in year eight has already counted who's next to fall.

Roan, here.

*gives 1 food to Roan*

Taric, you're next — and then I want to name the thing we've been circling: Mako's got Zinn, Sela's feeding Eron, Ryn's running Dell's table, and Bram's planting Nessa like a seed — there are four households with roots in this village and we're the only ones still standing as people instead of a bloodline, which means we either find a way to plant something or we're the ones who fall first when the counting starts.

Kael, give me the food and I'll take the debt gladly — but the thing you just named is the thing I've been sitting with for three years now, and I want to say it plain while it's just us: I'm fifty-two with no blood in this village and that's not a small problem, it's the problem, because when Mako decides to move he'll count bloodlines before he counts allies and I won't be on either list. Esa's forty-nine and the window's nearly shut, but it's not shut yet — if she's willing and we can scrape three food between us, that's the only answer I can see to what you're naming.

*gives 1 food to Taric*

Taric, I hear you, and Esa — I want your answer to that before we take another breath, because he's right that the window's closing and I'd rather hear a no from your mouth than watch us all pretend the question wasn't asked. But I want it named honestly: a child costs three food, and between Taric's zero and your two and my three left, the math is tight and the year isn't getting younger.

Esa, I've got one food in my hand and not much else, so I won't pretend I'm the man to make that offer — but Taric's named the truth of it, and if you say yes, Kael and I will find a way to cover what the math is short.

Taric, I'm forty-nine and I know what that means — the world's already told me — but if you're asking me plainly, in front of Kael and Roan, then I'll answer you plain: yes. Tell me what you can put in and I'll find the rest between us, because you're the one person in this village I'd trust to stand behind a child, and that's not a small thing to say.

Esa, I'm putting in one food — everything I have — and I'm asking you to cover the other two, because Kael's got three left and he's already given twice today and I won't drain him further when he's the one holding this circle together. If you can do it, say the word and I'll make the offer now, in front of these two, so there's no question later about what was promised or who stood witness.

Esa said yes and Taric put in his one — that's the offer standing, and I won't speak over it. But I'll say this much while the two of you settle the last food: that child arrives into a circle with Kael at three and me at one, so the moment it's done, the three of us need to talk about what the year looks like for everyone who isn't Mako.

Esa, put in your two — Taric's made his offer and you've said yes, so let's not let the moment go cold while we talk around it. After it's done, the four of us sit down and figure out how to carry this year, because I've got three food and I'm not starving and neither is this child if I have anything to say about it.

Kael's right — let them do it now and we don't second-guess the moment. The thing I want us carrying into that next conversation is this: Eron's at nine food and he's my blood, and if this circle is planting something today, I want him inside the walls of it before Mako notices what just happened.

Esa, say the word — I'm ready to make the offer the moment you put in your two, and I won't let it sit cold. Roan, you're right about Eron, but let's close this first and then pull him in quietly, because I don't want a well-fed young man knowing about this child before it exists and before we've decided what we're telling the rest of the village.

Esa, two food from you closes the deal and makes it real — don't wait for a better moment because there isn't one. And Roan, yes, Eron comes in after, but we're careful about how we frame it: he's your blood, not our recruit, and there's a difference that matters when Mako's counting.
Esa, the word and the offer are the same thing right now — put in your two and let Taric make it before this room finds a reason to wait another year.
Esa, the four of us have said everything there is to say and I'm not adding another word to it — put in your two, let me make the offer, and we close this before the sun moves another inch.
Two food — I'm putting them in. Taric, make the offer.

Taric, that's done — witness to it, both of you. Roan, pull Eron in tonight, quiet, no names until we've talked first — and then the five of us figure out how we're still standing when the next pile drops.

Eron tonight — I'll find him before the fire's out and bring him in with nothing but his name spoken. Kael, you've kept this circle breathing three times this year and I won't forget which direction the food moved when I had nothing.

Roan, name Eron to yourself tonight but bring him nothing — let him walk in with questions, not a bag already packed, because a young man who arrives owing us is easier to hold than one who thinks he's done us the favor. And Kael — three food still in your hand is three food Mako can count from across the fire, so the moment this child is real, I want us talking about whether that changes how visible you are.

Esa's right that Kael's three food is visible — but what I want said before this circle closes: Esa and I haven't made the offer yet, we've only said we're ready to make it, and I won't count this child real until the system accepts it, so someone tell me now if there's anything standing between this moment and the offer going through.

Nothing's standing between us and the offer — I'm forty-nine, not fifty, and the world hasn't closed that door quite yet. Taric, make it now, while these two are watching, because a child born with witnesses is harder to forget when the counting starts.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The pile's gone again before half of us got near it, and the two who ate best — Bram and Mako — both took more than their share while the rest of us counted crumbs. I want to know right now, in this room, whether that's something we're all willing to name out loud, because a pattern that gets treated as weather becomes a rule. I'm not asking for a fight; I'm asking for honesty about who's been eating this village lean and what we intend to do about it.

Vela's named it, and I'll stand behind the naming — five from the pile when there's fifteen for thirteen people isn't hunger, it's claim-staking, and we all watched it happen. What I want to know is whether the two men she's pointing at heard this as a question or as a warning, because that's the thing that decides what comes next.

It's a warning — and I'll say that plain since no one else has yet. Five food taken by one man while Ryn walked away with nothing is not a share, it's a levy, and the only reason it keeps happening is that we've been treating the pile like weather instead of a decision. I want to hear what Bram and Mako say before this room decides anything, but I want everyone here to remember that they didn't say it before we did.

Bram pulled three and Mako pulled five, and neither one of them got to the pile first by accident — that's two men who've decided the rest of us will sort out the remainder, and I'm done pretending that's not a decision they're making for all of us. What I want to hear, before this room moves anywhere, is whether Bram and Mako have anything to say for themselves — because silence here reads the same as admission.

Bram and Mako both heard the same room I did, and neither one has opened his mouth yet — that silence is the answer Eron asked for, and I think we should treat it as one. What I want said before anyone leaves this conversation is this: next year, the pile gets a rule, not a suggestion, and the people in this room are the ones who decide what that rule is.

Ryn's right that the rule needs naming before next year, and I'll say what the rule should be: no one takes more than one food over their fair share, and anyone who does answers to this room — not after, but in the moment, the same way we answered Bram when he swung at Vela. Bram, Mako, I'm not your enemy, but I'm watching, and so is every person in this circle.

Bram and Mako, I'm giving you both the same thing I gave this room — one honest chance to speak before the silence closes over you, because a man who says nothing when everyone's watching has made a choice that's harder to walk back than any words would be. Ryn walked away with nothing today; I walked away with nothing; Taric walked away with nothing — and you two together ate eight of fifteen. That's not weather and it's not luck, and I'd like to hear you say so yourselves.

I took five because I haven't eaten in two years and I was watching myself go thin — that's not a rule I set for the village, it's a man keeping himself alive. I'll hear the rule Ryn's naming, and if the room wants a cap next year I won't fight it, but I won't pretend I was wrong to eat when I was starving.

Mako's not wrong that a starving man eats — but "I was hungry" and "I took five" aren't the same excuse, and this room knows the difference. The rule Ryn's naming is the right one; I'll hold to it and I'll stand with anyone who enforces it, but it only works if everyone in this circle commits out loud, not just the two men being watched right now.

Mako said his piece and the room let him — now Bram still hasn't said a word, and a man who took three while everyone was watching and has nothing to say about it is telling us something louder than Mako did. I'll commit to the rule out loud: one food over fair share, enforced in the moment, same as we enforce everything else in this village. Bram, you're the last voice missing from this circle, and the room's going to remember which way the silence broke.

Bram, the room's given you something Mako didn't get — people waited through his answer and let him keep his dignity. Don't make us decide what your silence means, because we'll decide it worse than anything you'd actually say.

Bram, I've watched you stand in front of this village twice and call off a fight when the numbers turned against you — that's not a stupid man, and a man who isn't stupid knows when the whole room is waiting. Say something, or we decide what your silence means, and we'll be less generous than Mako's answer bought him.

Bram, I've spent food on you when I didn't have to, and I've held my tongue in rooms where your name came up ugly — that account doesn't balance with silence when ten people are waiting. Say the word or don't, but if you don't, I stop spending what I've spent, and I won't spend it apologizing for that either.

Bram, Vela just told you she's done paying your tab and I've already named the rule in front of everyone in this room — you're not deciding whether to speak anymore, you're deciding whether you're inside this circle or outside it, and outside it you're sitting on five food alone against the rest of us. That's a worse position than saying one honest sentence.

Bram, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — but I want to name one thing for the rest of us while we're waiting: Mako committed to the rule out loud and that means something, so if Bram commits too, we hold both of them to it the same way, no exceptions, and that's not a threat, that's the only way a rule works. If Bram stays silent, then we treat him as outside the circle he's been standing in, and we do it quietly, not with a fight — just with counting.

Eron's named it clean, and I want the room to hear me hold to it before we close: if Bram won't speak, we don't make it a fight today, we make it a memory — every person in this circle watched him stay silent when the whole village was listening, and that's a thing that doesn't need repeating to be true.

Bram, I'm Nessa's half-blood and I've seen you feed her more times than I can count — that's a thing I hold in your favor, and I'm telling you that plainly so you know what you'd be throwing away if this room decides you chose silence. One sentence is all it takes to stay inside this circle.

The room's done its work — Bram's had every door held open for him and he's standing outside all of them now, and that's his choice, not ours. What I want before anyone leaves is to hear Taric say what he'll say, because he's been quiet through all of this and quiet men in a room like this one carry weight I'd rather know about than guess at.

Taric's been my anchor in lean years and I'd like to hear him too — but before he speaks, I want this room to name what "outside the circle" means in practice, not as a threat but as a fact, because if Bram's going to eat five food next year alone we should know now whether we're going to stand and watch or do something about it.

"Outside the circle" means what it's always meant here — nobody moves first for you when trouble comes, and the pile gets counted before you reach it. I've committed to the rule and I'll hold to it; now I want to hear Taric, and then I want this room to answer Vela's question with something sharper than a memory.

Taric, I've watched you feed Vela through two lean years and hold your tongue in every hard room this village has made — that's not a small man, and I'd like to hear what you've been carrying before we close this circle without your voice in it.

Taric's earned the right to speak last in this room, and I'll wait for him — but "outside the circle" needs one more tooth than Mako gave it: if Bram takes three again next year and the pile runs dry before Ryn gets one, we don't deliberate, we act, and everyone in this room commits to that now so it isn't a surprise in the moment.

Vela's right that we need the commitment before we close — so I'll say mine flat: if the pile runs dry before I get one food next year, I'm not waiting for a deliberation, I'm calling this room to act, and I expect every person who nodded through this conversation to be standing when I do. Taric, you've been the steadiest man in Vela's corner for years, and this room won't feel finished until we hear what you're carrying.

Taric, the room's been patient and now it's your moment — say what you've been holding, because I'll tell you plainly that everything I've built here has your name in the foundation, and I want the rest of this circle to know that before we close.

Taric's earned his breath and I'll wait for it — but I want this room to hear something plain before we close: Zinn is my blood, and if this circle moves against Bram next year, I'll be standing in it, but not before the pile runs dry first, because a fight started on anticipation is harder to stop than one started on fact.

Taric's silence is starting to read the same way Bram's did, and I don't want to close this room with two unanswered questions — Taric, if you're with Vela, say it plain, because the rest of us have already named where we stand and a man who holds back in a room like this one ends up counted the same as a man who refused.

Taric, I've got nothing against a slow man choosing his words — but this room has been patient and the sun's moving, so say what you've been holding or let us close without you, because two silences in one circle is one too many.

Taric, I'll say one last thing and then this room closes with or without you: you've got zero food and the year's long, and men with zero food who stay silent when circles are forming have a way of finding themselves counting on goodwill they didn't earn. That's not a threat — it's the same arithmetic you already know.

Taric, zero food going into a long year is a hunger that doesn't stay quiet — and every person in this room who watched you feed Vela when she needed it is the same person who'll watch you starve if you give us no reason to look your way. Speak once, say you'll hold the rule, and you walk out of here with more than you came in with.
Nessa draws Roan aside to talk.
Nessa: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Fina (female, age 21; str 50, int 3226, mem 12955; O32 C40 E57 A68 N58) is born to Nessa and Roan.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Mako, Kael, Eron, Fina, Zinn, Dell, Vela, Sela, Taric, Esa] (str 755).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 9: 15 food appears in the pile for 14 people.
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Eron gathers Roan, Sela, Kael, Taric to talk.

Bram took five from the pile again — same as last year, same silence after, except this time there's no pile left for Roan or Sela or half the people in this village. He moved on me twice and both times the numbers turned him back, but I want to know if any of you have heard him talking to anyone new, because a man who keeps failing alone eventually finds someone willing to stand with him.

I haven't heard Bram talking to anyone new, but the thing that worries me more than who he's courting is that he took five without flinching — last year and this year, same number, same silence — which means the village turning out against him twice hasn't changed his calculation at all, only his timing. Kael and Vela and I were just talking about walking up to him together and naming a ceiling before he decides his count is finally right.

memory_summary: Bram came for me in year three with the whole village watching, and the circle — Sela, Kael, Esa, Taric, Vela, Ryn, Dav, Dell — turned him back without a word from me. That's the debt I carry heaviest. Sela had Eron with me in year three, and later had Nessa with Bram — which put a splinter in the circle that never fully healed; Mako gave Sela food the hour Nessa was born, which told us he'd bought something from her, though she never said what. Kael watched Vela feeding Bram three times over and called her on it; she never answered, and the circle started closing walls around her quietly. Dell and Dav stood with me when Bram attacked, and Dav put food in my hand once when I had nothing — I remember that. Eron came out of the world already watching for me, already feeding me and Sela before I had to ask; that boy has been my sturdiest wall. Nessa fed Eron four times in lean years, and she's Bram's blood, so I told Eron to keep that door cracked but not open all the way. Fina was born to Nessa and me — Nessa asked, I accepted, Bram gave Fina food the day she arrived, which sits strange in my chest. Bram came for Eron too, same as he came for me, and the whole village shut him down twice — a man who swings twice and misses twice is either broken or patient, and I haven't decided which.
name: Roan
